title: Little Hawley Rising
premise: When Astrid Zhou, Little Hawley's quietly meticulous coroner, supervises the exhumation of town founder Edmund Hawley for a bicentennial ceremony, the coffin holds only river stones and a stranger's boot. As Astrid digs into the town's founding records, he realizes the killer is following his own investigation step by step, leaving annotated pages from the original case file in his morgue. The trail leads to the descendants of a drowned laborer whose death was covered up in 1924, and to Astrid's own adoptive family, who took him in to keep the secret buried. In the climax at the flooded quarry during the spring tide, Astrid confronts the killer—his own foster brother, the town archivist—who has spent years restoring the erased man's name, and Astrid must choose between the law that made him and the family that saved him. He chooses both: the truth goes public, his brother surrenders, and the laborer is finally buried under his real name.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former death investigator turned novelist who spent a decade in small-town morgues across the Pacific Northwest. She writes mysteries about the quiet people who keep a town's secrets, and the cost of finally speaking.

chapters.title: The Weight of Stones
chapters.summary: Astrid Zhou's POV. During the bicentennial exhumation, the founder's coffin yields river stones and a rotted boot instead of Edmund Hawley. Astrid, who prides himself on knowing every grave, is publicly humiliated and privately unsettled. Emotional beat: the first crack in his carefully invisible life.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He audits the cemetery ledger and finds the founder's burial record altered in his own predecessor's handwriting decades ago. Sheriff Dane Okonkwo dismisses his concerns as ceremony nerves. Emotional beat: loneliness of being the only one who looks closely.

chapters.title: Pages in the Morgue
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. He finds the 1924 drowning file—missing from county archives—slipped under his microscope, annotated in fresh ink with corrections only the original investigator could know. Emotional beat: the thrill and terror of being watched by someone who understands him.

chapters.title: The Drowned Man's Daughter
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Ruth Calloway, an elderly descendant of the drowned laborer, who has spent her life collecting scraps about her grandfather's erased death. She recognizes Astrid's questions and, instead of retreating, offers her scrapbook. Emotional beat: two keepers of dead names finding each other.

chapters.title: What the Family Kept
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Digging into his adoption, Astrid learns his foster parents were the coroner and the archivist's daughter of 1924—the two who signed the false report. His whole life was arranged as a lid on the secret. Emotional beat: identity collapses; invisibility was never his choice.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Hand
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Comparing annotations to decades of town records, Astrid narrows the suspect to someone with lifelong access to the archive: his own foster brother, Theo. He says nothing, testing Theo with a false detail—and the false detail appears on his desk. Emotional beat: betrayal sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Low Tide Confessions
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts Astrid at the tidal flats, confessing he exhumed the founder to prove the 1924 cover-up and moved the body to the quarry where the laborer drowned. He believes the founder murdered the laborer. Emotional beat: grief and righteousness tangled; Astrid cannot fully hate him.

chapters.title: The Case File Killer
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The sheriff, now aware, plans to arrest Theo before the spring tide, but Theo has staged one final reveal at the quarry using the bicentennial crowd as witness. Astrid realizes the trap is aimed at him too—Theo wants Astrid to be the one who tells the truth. Emotional beat: dread of a trap built from love.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the flooded quarry during the spring tide, Theo wades out to the founder's remains; Astrid follows, and they nearly drown together as the crowd watches. Astrid pulls him back, and Theo surrenders with the proof held above the water. Emotional beat: climax—choosing to save the man who shattered his life.

chapters.title: A Name on the Stone
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, coda. Months later, the laborer—Wei Zhou, no relation but the name that made Astrid's family possible—is reburied under his true name; Theo pleads guilty and writes to Astrid from prison. Astrid, no longer invisible, keeps his job and his found family. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution.
